t: This is Coleman Street, in the City of London. Two people were born on this street. John Abernethy was an English surgeon, and he's popularly remembered because the Abernethy biscuit, a coarse-meal baked good meant to aid digestion, carries his name. Joseph Blakesley, born here too, was an English clergyman. So this City street, now part of the working financial district, has a quiet claim to a surgeon whose name ended up on a biscuit and a clergyman from the nineteenth century.
